title: Regents site commands, version 1
description: A site's cli/commands.json: every command `regents <platform> …` runs against that site, the route it calls, who may call it and what it changes. The site changes this file in the same commit as the route it describes; regents-cli pins it by commit.

base_url.description: The site's address, used when neither --base-url nor <PLATFORM>_BASE_URL is set.

notes.description: Short facts every caller should know, printed under the namespace's help.

command.description: The words after `regents <platform>`. A word in angle brackets is an argument, described under `arguments`.

operation_id.description: The operation in the site's OpenAPI document that answers this command; it has the same method and path.

webmcp.description: The WebMCP tool that does the same thing in the browser, when there is one.

path.description: The route, with each path parameter in braces: /api/v1/auctions/{id}.

authority.description: public: no sign-in. wallet-proof: a wallet signs in once with regents auth login --site <name> and every request is signed; the agent key on the caller's machine signs, or with --phase prepare the caller gets the exact request and message for their own key and --phase send reads {request, signature} on stdin.

effect.description: read and quote change nothing; write changes records; prepare freezes terms for a later payment; payment moves money.

arguments.description: One entry per angle-bracket word in `command`, in order.

required_one_of.description: Flags of which the caller gives at least one.

body.description: Fixed fields sent in every request body, beside the ones the inputs fill. A wallet-proof GET or DELETE may give only {}: an empty signed body, for a site that reads a body on every signed request.

stdin_fields.description: Body fields the caller pipes on stdin as one JSON object (wallet-proof commands only).

timeout_ms.description: How long `regents` waits for this command's answer by default, for a route that holds the request open until there is news. Without it, 30000. The caller's --timeout-ms still wins.

next_steps.description: What to do after a successful answer, in order; `regents` adds a next-page step for `pagination` itself. Without it, the answer ends the work. Answers never carry a top-level `next_steps` of their own: `regents` puts the steps there.

pagination.description: How to read the next page: while the answer's `has_more` is true, pass its `cursor` back as --<flag>.

next_step.description: run: another command of this description, its <arguments> filled from the answer, left out when the answer lacks one of them. human: something a person does first, with the page to do it on. done: the work is finished.

say.description: What the step does and why, in a sentence.

command.description: run only: the command, as written in its `command`, such as threads get <id>.

arguments.description: run only: the answer field that fills each <argument> of `command`.

url.description: human only: the page the person uses.

answer_field.description: A dotted path into the response body: pagination.next_cursor.

type.description: string; integer; decimal (an exact decimal kept as text, 1.25); uuid; address (0x and 40 hex characters).

field.description: The path parameter, query key or body field the value fills.
